summary.headline: SKF India Q4 FY26 sales rose 3% QoQ to INR 5.55 bn, but PBT margin fell to about 9% after Q3 one-off gains; management guides 11-12% PBT margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026) sales were a record INR 5.55 bn, up about 3% QoQ and about 14.8% YoY, driven by cars, 2-wheelers and powertrains, with a drop in distribution. Profit before tax margin fell to about 9% as Q3 had one-off gains from forex, fixed-deposit interest and employee cost provision reversals. FY26 sales grew about 12.7% to INR 20.3 bn with OE up about 20%, while full-year PBT margin fell to about 12.3% on demerger costs, mix and discounts. Management pointed to 11-12% PBT margin as the near-term sustainable level and said cash conversion was about 85%.

segments.name: Automotive OE
segments.commentary: About 66% of Q4 sales and the main growth driver, with FY26 OE sales up about 20%. Management said the growth came from OEM, and OEM margins are structurally different from aftermarket.

segments.name: Distribution / aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q4 sales; declined YoY in FY26. Management said volumes were held flat but net sales fell due to discounts to defend share against competition.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 8% of Q4 sales; broadly steady but slightly lower. Domestic demand is prioritised given limited capacity, and overseas demand is served from nearby plants.

segments.name: SKF Industrial (traded)
segments.commentary: About 6% of Q4 sales. Automotive buys traded product from SKF Industrial (medium DGBB and tapered roller bearings) to cover capacity shortfall; traded purchases were about 15-20% of revenue in Q3-Q4 per analyst.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable company-level PBT margin of about 11-12% in the near term; long-term focus is on improving it further.
Management expects margins to return toward prior levels after a couple of quarters once one-offs and transition costs fade.
Demerger costs in Q4 were minimal and no further demerger-related costs are expected.
Raw material (steel) cost pass-through has begun with a couple of OEMs and aftermarket; near-term gross margin pressure from pass-through lag acknowledged.
Automotive revenue growth expected at about 6-8% CAGR to 2028, per management.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR 500 crore over FY26-FY28, with about INR 200 crore in FY26, spilling into Q1 FY27.
Capex aims to bring trading from SKF Industrial into in-house automotive capacity; this does not add revenue beyond existing trading revenue.
Automotive is short of capacity; two new product lines are coming up at Haridwar in 2026.
Automotive plant in Pune is common with SKF Industrial; SKF India receives rent and service charges for space used by Industrial until its new factory is ready.
Localisation above 90% in automotive, which management says will continue.
demand_pricing: Strong order book and wins in electric motors and wheel-hub bearings, with launches in FY27; order book described as running to about 2030.
EV share of 2-wheeler business is about 50% per MD; EV revenue mix is about 6% of 2-wheeler and about 4% of passenger vehicle sales.
Aftermarket discounts used to hold share against competition; price increases in aftermarket have started.
Top 5 customers are close to 50% of revenue; top 10 about 70%. Bajaj is the largest customer, followed by Mahindra and Tata.
White spaces named: unitised wheel bearings for SCV/LCV and low-friction, low-weight transmission products for CAFE-3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin going forward into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 11-12% PBT margin is achievable near term; Q4 demerger costs were small and Q3 one-off gains distorted the comparison.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said steel-linked price increases are recoverable under OEM agreements; recovery has started with a couple of customers, with aftermarket increases also starting. Lag means near-term gross margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What are the arrangements with SKF Industrial (trading, rent, service charges)?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading mainly flows from Industrial to auto due to capacity shortfall; SKF India receives rent and service charges from Industrial. Annual amount not quantified. Royalty and trademark fees unchanged from pre-demerger settlement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix by segment and customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Segment mix by end-market not disclosed. Top 5 customers about 50%, top 10 about 70%. Distribution about 20% (about 28% excluding exports).

qa_highlights.question: Concerns about reduced disclosure and margin comparability post demerger.
qa_highlights.answer: Management took the feedback, said it will try to give more detail, and said no royalty change occurred. It argued that no listed pure-play auto bearing peer exists for benchmarking.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from lag in steel pass-through to OEMs and aftermarket price discounting.
Trading purchases from SKF Industrial are a large share of revenue; the related cost and the rent/service-charge arrangement are not quantified.
Management did not provide a breakdown of margin compression between one-offs, demerger costs and transfer arrangements, despite shareholder requests.
Net working capital and cash conversion (85%) need to normalise in FY27.
Capacity shortage limits export volumes and forces reliance on trading.
Investor perception: an analyst said post-demerger disclosure has weakened and margins are below pre-demerger levels of 16-17% EBITDA.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the EV pipeline and the 11-12% margin target, but cautious and at times evasive on margin bridge and transfer arrangements with SKF Industrial. Management did not quantify several items and repeatedly described the margin dip as transitional.
key_quotes: Our profitability for the quarter dropped to about 9%, which is primarily impacted by one-off factors, and these factors are expected to normalize as we move forward.
we could be looking at 11-12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.
So, from '26 to '28, we have around INR 500 crores investment, which will go through each year.
We don't trade. We don't bring too much of our bearings from overseas and sell it.

financial_highlights.change: Down about 770 bps vs Q3 (per MD's remarks), Q3 included one-off gains

financial_highlights.value: Up about 4.6% in Q4 (QoQ); improved 3.7% for FY26 YoY
financial_highlights.change: Q4 rise attributed to one-offs, expected to normalise

adds.what: Two new automotive product lines at Haridwar

growth.why: Management guides automotive revenue CAGR of about 6-8% to 2028 and 11-12% PBT margin, backed by a strong order book (EV motors, wheel hubs, running to about 2030), two Haridwar product lines due in 2026, and about INR 500 crore capex over FY26-28, though no specific capacity-to-revenue bridge is given and automotive is capacity-constrained.
